Rates that depend on mapped regimes

Source: R/kernels_regime.R
k_regime.Rd

Brownian motion whose rate depends on a discrete regime painted on the tree, as in multi-rate Brownian motion models (O'Meara et al. 2006). The regimes come from the tree: give phylo_gp() a stochastic character map (a simmap from phytools::make.simmap(), or a tree painted with phytools::paintSubTree()), whose mapped.edge holds the time each branch spends in each regime. Regimes may change along a branch.

Usage

k_regime(
  states = NULL,
  reference = NULL,
  rate_scale = 1,
  lower = 0.001,
  upper = 1000
)

Arguments

states

Optional regime names. By default, all regimes mapped on the tree (sorted).

reference

Regime whose rate is 1; by default the first of states.

rate_scale

Standard deviation of the lognormal priors of the relative rates.

lower, upper

Bounds of the relative rates.

Value

A kernel component.

Details

Each edge accumulates variance sigma^2 * sum_r rate_r * t_r, where t_r is the time it spends in regime r. The rate of the reference regime is 1, so sigma is its standard deviation per unit time and the rate_ parameters are the rates of the other regimes relative to it. The kernel is branch-wise, so it keeps the linear-time likelihood, leave-one-out, prediction and ancestral states, and it can be fitted by maximum likelihood. In Bayesian fits the relative rates get lognormal priors centred on 1.

To integrate over uncertainty in the history of the regimes, fit a sample of stochastic maps (a multiSimmap) with phylo_gp_trees().

References

O'Meara B.C., Ané C., Sanderson M.J., Wainwright P.C. 2006. Testing for different rates of continuous trait evolution using likelihood. Evolution. 60:922–933.

Huelsenbeck J.P., Nielsen R., Bollback J.P. 2003. Stochastic mapping of morphological characters. Systematic Biology. 52:131–158.

Revell L.J. 2012. phytools: An R package for phylogenetic comparative biology (and other things). Methods in Ecology and Evolution. 3:217–223.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
tr <- phytools::pbtree(n = 100, scale = 1)
Q <- matrix(c(-1, 1, 1, -1), 2, 2, dimnames = list(c("a", "b"), c("a", "b")))
smap <- phytools::sim.history(tr, Q)
fit <- phylo_gp(y ~ 1, d, smap, k_regime() + k_white(), method = "optimize")
} # }
